summary.headline: The Southborough Tricentennial Committee approved up to $25,000 for the Firemen's Muster and reviewed plans for banners, tours, and anniversary events.
summary.summary: The committee advanced planning across several 2027 anniversary events and community projects. Members voted to cap the Firemen's Muster budget at $25,000 and discussed banner sizing and hardware for village poles with an estimated cost of $3,500 to $5,000. Updates were also provided on school tours, a town coloring book, historic house tours, drone show contracts, time capsule coordination with local scouts, and commemorative tree donations.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved the meeting minutes from May 13, 2026, and later adjourned the meeting.
key_details: Minutes of May 13, 2026, approved unanimously.

topics.title: Town banners and pole brackets
topics.summary: Members reviewed pole measurements and photos from neighboring towns to establish banner specifications for Southborough's villages. The committee settled on 18-by-36-inch banners with stainless steel screw clamp brackets to avoid damaging utility poles. With estimated costs of around $70 per set, the total estimated cost for 40 to 50 banners is $3,500 to $5,000.
key_details: Banner dimensions set at 18 inches wide by 36 inches high.
Estimated budget range between $3,500 and $5,000 for approximately 40 to 50 banners.
Banners will be placed in Fayville, Cordaville, Southville, and Main Street.
Final design options will be presented in July for manufacturing before September.
topics.outcome: Committee agreed on banner dimensions and a $3,500 to $5,000 budget target.

topics.title: History in Bloom, school tours, and family events
topics.summary: The committee reviewed progress on educational and youth events. The Southborough Garden Club confirmed dates for 'History in Bloom' for April 15-17, 2027. St. Mark's School faculty is developing a tour script and identifying historical artifacts for public display, and local historian Nick Noble drafted a town history coloring book for children ages 5 to 8.
key_details: History in Bloom scheduled for April 15-17, 2027.
St. Mark's School working script will be written over the summer for student-led tours.
Children's coloring book printing estimated at a few hundred dollars for distribution at Fay School and potentially schools and libraries.

topics.title: Oral history, graveyard tour, and house tour updates
topics.summary: Volunteers are collecting oral history interviews from current and former residents, with formatting and historical photo matching underway. A committee member is coordinating with the Nipmuc tribe regarding sensitive historical sites for the graveyard tour. Work is also advancing on draft homeowner and ticket holder agreements for the historic house tour.
key_details: Oral history project continues to record interviews and source photographs.
Coordination underway with the Nipmuc tribe regarding graveyard tour sites.
House tour participant agreements are being prepared for Town Counsel review.
topics.outcome: Draft contracts being finalized for legal review.

topics.title: Parade planning and drone show contract
topics.summary: The committee reviewed a three-page draft of participation rules and standards for the anniversary parade, covering safety, breakdowns, and animal waste management. Members also discussed a pending contract for a drone light show and noted the need to confirm whether municipal procurement bidding rules apply.
key_details: Parade standards and participant contracts will be distributed to prospective entrants.
Town Administrator must execute formal municipal event contracts.
Drone show contract is currently being reviewed for legal language and procurement requirements.
topics.outcome: Committee will circulate the parade contract to participants and check procurement rules on the drone show.

topics.title: Firemen's Muster budget and sponsorship standards
topics.summary: The committee voted to approve an initial budget cap of up to $25,000 for the Firemen's Muster event. Discussion centered on the return of Southborough's historic first fire engine, the Falcon, to the fire club's museum, and securing commitments from two live bands. Members also debated the boundary between town tricentennial branding, corporate event sponsorships, and club fundraising.
key_details: Voted 6-0 to approve a muster budget not to exceed $25,000 at this time.
The historic 'Falcon' hand tub fire engine has been returned to the Southborough club for restoration.
Two musical acts have committed to perform for up to four hours, with staging arrangements pending.
Guidelines will be established regarding how corporate sponsors and 501(c)(3) funds are recognized on promotional materials.
topics.why_it_matters: Commits up to $25,000 in anniversary celebration funding for the town-wide muster event and establishes promotional rules.

topics.title: Time capsule and youth organization outreach
topics.summary: Committee member Eric updated the group on plans for a 50-year time capsule to be sealed during the tricentennial. Organizers are creating intake guidelines and preservation standards for community submissions and plan to partner with local Boy Scout troops to help manage and inventory items.
key_details: Time capsule designed to preserve community items for 50 years.
Outreach underway to local Boy Scout troops (Troop 1 and Troop 92) to assist with logistics.
topics.outcome: Outreach to scout leaders to continue over the summer.

topics.title: Glow SoBo, legacy trees, and brick fundraiser
topics.summary: The Glow SoBo working group is evaluating decorative uplighting for the Town House and the Southborough Library with a landscape lighting contractor. For the legacy tree project, a local supplier offered to donate trees to be planted in each of the four villages in fall 2026 or spring 2027 in consultation with the Tree Warden and DPW. Meanwhile, roughly 100 commemorative bricks have been sold toward a 300-brick fundraising goal.
key_details: Landscape company will assess exterior lighting for the Library and Town House.
Tree donations offered for all four villages; sites and species to be coordinated with the Tree Warden and DPW.
Approximately 100 commemorative bricks sold to date toward a 300-brick target.
The committee is seeking two additional members to fill vacancies on the nine-member board.
topics.outcome: Site visits and outreach will proceed through the summer.

votes.motion: Approve a budget not to exceed $25,000 at this time for the Firemen's Muster based on the event outline.
